title: kv-cache-eviction-defrag-spillover-scheduling-improvements
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and uncoordinated spillover have been a recurring source of tail latency and OOMs in high-concurrency continuous-batching workloads. This PR implements coordinated background defragmentation, improved eviction priority heuristics that consider fragment size and recency, and a lightweight spillover paging scheduler that reduces synchronous I/O during hot spikes. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce a compacting defragmenter that runs opportunistically when GPU memory is under pressure; it coalesces adjacent free regions and compacts large inactive KV entries to reduce fragmentation without impacting critical inference paths. 2) Eviction policy rewrite: add weighted score = alpha*LRU + beta*fragment_penalty + gamma*size_penalty; tunable defaults selected after offline traces. 3) Paging/spillover scheduler: background pager that batches spill I/O and respects per-model quotas to avoid head-of-line blocking; integrates with existing continuous-batching scheduler to prioritize requests that hit cached prefixes. 4) Runtime kernel guardrails: a small set of kernel-level checks to abort defrag passes that would exceed per-device CPU/GPU utilization budgets. 5) Telemetry and rollout flags: new metrics (kv.fragmentation_ratio, kv.defrag_cycles, kv.spill_io_batch_size) and feature-flag controlled rollout for Dedicated customers. Backwards compatibility: behavior is feature-flag gated, defaults enabled in staging and can be toggled per-tenant. Benchmarking: internal perf harness shows median token latency improvement of 6-9% under high-fragmentation traces and 20-35% reduction in OOM incidents on synthetic multi-tenant workloads. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-2314) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Benchmarks and perf runs - [x] Telemetry dashboards - [x] Feature flags for staged rollout Rollout plan: enable in staging for 48h, canary to 10% Dedicated capacity, monitor kv.* metrics and latency P95. If kv.defrag_cycles > threshold or spill_io_latency regresses, rollback flag. Notes: defragmentation is designed to be cooperative: it yields to inference threads and uses small compaction windows to avoid latency cliffs. The eviction weights are exposed via config map for quick tuning.
commits: feat(kv): add compacting defragmenter and scheduler integration
perf(kv): rewrite eviction scoring to include fragment/size penalties
test(kv): add unit tests for defrag and eviction scoring
infra: expose kv defrag and pager flags in feature flag service
docs: add telemetry and rollout instructions to ops playbook
review_comments: Diego: Asked for clarity on defrag CPU/GPU budget enforcement and suggested adding a safety valve to abort long-running compactions. Response: added kernel guardrails and unit tests that emulate compaction timeouts. Priya: Requested telemetry for per-model spill IO and suggested exposing tuning knobs for beta users. Response: added kv.spill_io_batch_size and per-model quotas. Liam: Verified benchmarks and asked to include a regression test that simulates high-concurrency spike; author added integration test and updated bench results.
ci_checks: CI pipeline: linux-build (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration-tests (pass), perf-harness (pass on staging traces), lint (pass), security-scan (pass). Note: first CI run failed on lint due to style in eviction_policy.h and was fixed in second commit.
bench_summary: Staging perf harness: under synthetic 2000 qps mixed-length sequences with 45% small-cache hit rate and high fragmentation traces: median token latency reduced 6-9%, P95 improved 4-6%, OOM rate reduced from 0.12% -> 0.03%. Dedicated cluster canary (10% capacity): observed stable latencies and decreased KV memory churn metrics.
release_notes: Runtime: KV cache improvements — background defragmentation, adaptive eviction scoring, and batched spillover paging. Reduces tail latency and OOMs under fragmented workloads. Feature-flag gated for staged rollout.
